items.prompt: Explain the difference between opportunity cost and adding together every rejected option.
items.canonical_answer: Opportunity cost concerns the next-best feasible alternative. Adding every rejected option counts sacrifices that could not all have been chosen instead.
marking_guidance: Difference (1): opportunity cost is the next-best feasible alternative. Contrast/test (1): exclude the sum of all rejected alternatives because only one can be the next-best option.

items.prompt: Explain opportunity cost using these invented production possibilities for the fictional Otjomuise school garden in Windhoek. With its fixed land and labour it can grow weekly combinations (bean crates, tomato crates): (0,12), (2,8), (4,4), (6,0). Plot beans horizontally and tomatoes vertically. Explain the movement from (2,8) to (4,4), assuming efficient use and unchanged resources and technology.
items.canonical_answer: Label both axes in crates per week, plot all four points and connect the linear frontier. Moving from two to four bean crates sacrifices four tomato crates. Each extra bean crate costs two tomato crates over this interval. This is a movement along the frontier with unchanged productive capacity, illustrating the next-best feasible output forgone, not a shift of the frontier.
marking_guidance: Axes/labels (1): beans and tomatoes in crates per week. Initial position / original curve (2): all four supplied combinations accurately (1), straight line through them (1). Change/control (1): movement along the existing frontier from (2,8) to (4,4), resources unchanged. Explanation (2): four tomato crates forgone (1), because those resources are reassigned to two extra bean crates (1). Interpretation (1): two tomato crates per extra bean crate; this is the sacrifice along the supplied frontier.

items.prompt: Evaluate a learning centre’s choice to use its room for reading support. It can run either reading support or computer skills this term, has applicants for both, and its stated priority is learners struggling with reading.
items.canonical_answer: Reading support directly serves the stated priority. Computer learning is nevertheless forgone, so the rejected group has a real opportunity cost. Reading support is justified if the reading need is more urgent under that priority. An additional volunteer able to run computer skills at another time could change the feasible choices and therefore the judgement.

Argument against/limitation (2): computer learning is forgone (1), reducing access for the waiting computer group (1). Condition/trade-off (1): the relative urgency of reading under the stated objective. Judgement/conclusion (2): choose reading on that priority (1), but reconsider the feasible combination if an additional volunteer and time slot remove this particular sacrifice (1).

items.prompt: Invented Windhoek teaching data: Otjomuise Learning Centre, with a N$600 room budget, has one available afternoon and sufficient staff for one activity. Its priority ranking is reading support first, computer skills second and art third. Describe the scarcity and choice involved, including opportunity cost (6). Explain why the computer group rather than both rejected activities supplies the opportunity cost (7). Discuss whether choosing reading support remains justified if an additional volunteer can provide computer skills at a different time without reducing reading support (7).
items.canonical_answer: Description: one afternoon and limited staff constrain three desired uses; choosing reading support sacrifices the next-best feasible computer group (6). The same afternoon and staff cannot run reading and computing together. Choosing reading therefore removes computing from the feasible uses of those resources. Computing ranks above art and could have run instead of reading, so its benefit is the next-best feasible sacrifice. Art is lower ranked. Adding both rejected benefits would count activities that could not jointly replace reading under this constraint (7). Discussion: reading meets the stated priority, but computer learning has a value; an additional volunteer and separate time change feasibility. Retain reading while checking that the new arrangement genuinely avoids displacing another valued activity. Develop both sides and justify the decision within seven marks (7).
marking_guidance: Context/data description (6): one scarce afternoon (1) and limited staff (1); three desired uses (1); reading chosen (1); computing next-best feasible use (1); computing benefit forgone (1). Mechanism/explanation (7): same resource cannot support both uses (1); reading choice removes computing (1); computing ranks above art (1); computing is feasible (1); its benefit is sacrificed (1); art is not the next-best option (1); adding computing and art incorrectly aggregates mutually exclusive alternatives (1). Both sides and judgement (7): priority supports reading (1), urgent need makes it valuable (1); computer learning has a benefit (1) lost under the old constraint (1); volunteer plus separate time changes feasibility (1); retain reading and add computing if no other valued use is displaced (1); explicitly test that condition before concluding both can run (1). Marks allocation 6+7+7=20.
